body:
## What happens

On a page built by `make_page.py`, pressing **Copy my reply** in the Claude desktop app's browser pane does nothing: no copy, no message. aj reported it on 2026-10-18 on `docs/plans/2026-10-18-tree-sitter-trial.html`.

## Cause, checked in the pane

The pane loads a local page as a `data:` URL. That is not a secure context (`window.isSecureContext` is `false`, origin `null`), so `navigator.clipboard` is `undefined`. The button's handler in `templates/handover-page.html` (the `document.getElementById("copy").onclick` line) calls `navigator.clipboard.writeText(...)` directly. That throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'writeText')` before the promise exists, so its `.catch` fallback, which selects the reply and says to copy it by hand, never runs. `document.queryCommandSupported('copy')` is `true` in the same pane.

## The fix

In the template's copy handler: when `navigator.clipboard` is missing, or `writeText` rejects, select the reply and call `document.execCommand("copy")`; say "Copied" when it returns true, and fall back to "The reply is selected; copy it by hand" when it returns false. Every page built before the fix keeps the bug until it is rebuilt.

## Depends on

Nothing.

## Depended on by

Every proposal and QA page aj answers from the browser pane.

## Done when

On a page built after the fix and opened in the app's browser pane, pressing Copy my reply puts the reply on the clipboard and shows "Copied", checked by pasting it. A check in `make_page.py`'s visual check, or a `verify.py` case, presses the button on a page loaded without a secure context and finds the status text set.

## What happened

On 21 October 2026 I built a proposal page for aj with `make_page.py build`. It carried the approval phrase `Build plan approved: canna-stock-finder criteria` and asked aj to pick a data source (A, B or C). The builder accepted it, and its visual check passed in light and dark mode.

The page had no choice buttons and no **Copy my reply** box. Two mistakes caused it, and the builder caught neither:

1. The content set `"kind": "summary"`, copied from `templates/decision-summary.page.json`. That template is for summarising decisions already made, so it has no `choices`.
2. The A/B/C question was written as text inside a `changes` item instead of in `choices`. `build` runs `page.setdefault("choices", [])` (scripts/make_page.py, the build command), so an empty choice list is silently allowed.

The editor pass did not catch it either, because it reviews wording, not page structure.

## What should happen

`build` refuses, with exit code 2 and a message naming the fix, when:

- the approval phrase starts with `Design approved:` or `Build plan approved:` and `choices` is empty or missing, unless the content sets an explicit flag such as `"no_choices_reason": "<why>"`; or
- `"kind": "summary"` is combined with a `Design approved:` or `Build plan approved:` phrase, since a summary page cannot carry the picks that phrase is followed by.

A useful extra check: warn when a `changes` detail contains option letters such as "A (suggested)" or "A:" followed by "B:", because that usually means a question was put in the wrong section.

## Depends on

Nothing. Related to #309, which covers the builder accepting any approval line; this issue is about the page body, not the phrase.

Nothing yet.

- A content file with a `Build plan approved:` phrase and no `choices` makes `build` exit with code 2 and a message naming `choices`.

## What happened

On 21 October 2026, in a cloud session driven from the Claude mobile app, aj replied `Build plan approved: canna-stock-finder criteria 1A 2* 3* 4A`. The UserPromptSubmit note on that message, as on every other message aj sent in the session, was:

> Design loop: this message is a helper's report or a notification, not aj, so it moved nothing.

A builder subagent was then refused by the design-loop lock with the stage still at Design.

## Why

In this surface, every genuine message from aj reaches UserPromptSubmit with a `<system-reminder>` block in front of it (it carries his timezone and send time). `_RELAYED_PROMPT_RE` in `scripts/house_rules/core.py` treats any prompt containing `<system-reminder>` as relayed, so `_is_relayed_prompt` returns True and `_loop_scope_note` in `scripts/house_rules/design_loop.py` returns before reading the approval. "skip design" is read in the same place, so it cannot get through either.

## What should happen

A prompt counts as relayed only if it is relayed: for example, when it starts with a notification or hand-back marker, or when the payload's `origin` is not human. A `<system-reminder>` block in front of aj's own text should be stripped before the approval, skip and bare-approval patterns are matched.

## Depends on

Nothing.

## Depended on by

Any build in a session driven from the Claude app.

## Done when

- A prompt of `<system-reminder>The user's timezone is America/Edmonton.</system-reminder>Build plan approved: demo` moves the stage to Build in a test.
- A prompt that starts with `[Subagent hand-back]` or `<task-notification>` still moves nothing.

Part of #396 (Background work tracking: every layer of delegated work is one tap away), step 1 of 5.

## What happened

On 26 October 2026, in the PlunderSpell project on claude.ai, a project thread ran its work through a separate Remote Control session on aj's PC (a Claude Code session started on aj's own machine by the thread's `start_remote_control` tool). aj wanted to read that session's raw transcript, but could not find it: the session list on aj's device showed "No active sessions".

The project's coordinator found the session id only by calling the `remote_control_status` tool, which returned an id starting `cse_`. Swapping the `cse_` prefix for `session_` and opening that session's page on claude.ai worked: aj confirmed the page loads and shows the transcript. (The id itself is left out of this issue: no session or artifact link goes into git or GitHub, per aj's rule of 27 October 2026.)

So the transcript exists and is reachable, but only when aj thinks to ask and an agent knows the trick.

## What should happen

Whenever a project thread works through a Remote Control session, aj gets that session's transcript link automatically, in the thread only (never in git or GitHub):

1. As soon as the session starts (the `start_remote_control` result says `started` or `already_running`), the thread looks up the session id with `remote_control_status` and posts the transcript link to aj in the thread, titled "Transcript of the session on your PC", with the raw id beside it.
2. The link is also attached to that message as a link output, so it stays in the project's Library, and it goes in the header line of the thread's checklist (design choice 2A).
3. If a thread starts a new session later, the new link is posted the same way; an old link is never silently replaced.
4. If the id can't be read (the status tool fails or returns no id), the thread says so in the same message, naming what failed, instead of saying nothing.

Built as a PostToolUse hook on `mcp__hearthbot__start_remote_control` (handler `rclink`) that tells the thread to fetch the id and post the link. It does nothing outside a project thread (`CLAUDE_CODE_PROJECTS_SESSION` unset). The Stop check that blocks a turn missing the link is step 4.

## Open question, answered

The `cse_` to `session_` swap held on a second session on 27 October 2026 (the design thread for #396). It is still undocumented, so the raw id always travels with the link.

## Depends on

Nothing.

## Depended on by

Step 4 of #396 (the Stop check for links owed) and step 5 (docs, version and QA page).

## Done when

- A verify.py case feeds `rclink` a recorded `start_remote_control` result saying `started` and checks the instruction names `remote_control_status`, the link title and attaching the link.
- A second case checks a result saying `asked` produces no instruction, and a third checks that nothing fires when `CLAUDE_CODE_PROJECTS_SESSION` is unset.
- In a project thread that starts a Remote Control session, the first reply after the start carries a working transcript link, attached as a link output, without aj asking, and aj opens it from the Claude app.

## What happens

In a Claude cloud session (the desktop app driving a cloud container), the design loop treats every message aj types as "a helper's report or a notification, not aj". Typed approvals such as `skip design` or `Build plan approved: <feature>` move nothing, so source edits stay locked for the whole session.

The cloud surface puts a note in front of each user message, wrapped in a `<system-reminder>` tag, for example: `<system-reminder>The user's timezone is America/Edmonton (UTC-06:00). Message sent at ...</system-reminder>skip design`.

```
_is_relayed_prompt('skip design')                                         -> False
_is_relayed_prompt('<system-reminder>The user\'s timezone is ...</system-reminder>skip design') -> True
```

Strip leading `<system-reminder>...</system-reminder>` blocks from the prompt before the relayed check and the approval-phrase match, so the text aj actually typed is what gets judged. A message made only of a system reminder should still count as relayed.

body:
Handoff for a new session. aj asked for this on 2026-11-02 and asked that it be enforced in every project, not just one. It takes in #139, which proposed the builder rule on 2026-10-03 and was never built, so the same failure happened again.

## What happened

In Ajw2003/PlunderSpell, issue #569, on 2026-11-02, a builder subagent ran one co-op gap check 12 times in 23 minutes. Each run opens Play mode and a second game window on aj's screen. Several runs went on repairing the check rather than the code. aj: "the other session writes a broken test and spends a ton of time just trying to fix the test instead of the code itself". The parent had written a hard number from that check as the done-when, with no limit on runs. In #238, on 2026-10-02, a builder made 8 such runs.

A rule in a project's memory doesn't reach this: builders never see it, and it only covers that project on that PC.

## What to build

Both go in `plugins/house-rules`.

1. **Builder rules, in `agents/builder.md`.** It limits test suites but says nothing about in-game or harness runs. Start from the wording in #139, and add:
   - At most two runs of any one in-game, end-to-end or harness check. After a second failure, stop and report, naming what failed.
   - Never change a check to make it pass. If the check itself looks wrong, stop and report that.
   - Read the code for the cause between runs.
   - A number from a check is evidence for the report. It doesn't decide when the work is done, unless the plan says so.

   Add a matching line to `rules/detail/delegate-execution.md`, so a parent doesn't write a measured number as a builder's only finish line, and checks on a running builder at about 10 minutes.

2. **A hook that enforces it.** `hooks/hooks.json` already runs a `PreToolUse` guard on `Bash|PowerShell`, through `scripts/run.sh guard`. Extend that route, or add one beside it, to count runs of the same check in a session and refuse the third, with a message telling the agent to stop and report. Refused means blocked, as the guard does for commits on `main`.

## Questions to settle in the design

The house rules apply: bring aj a page with options and a suggestion before building.

- **What counts as the same check?** Candidates: the same script path under a project's tools folder, or the same normalised command. It must not catch ordinary commands such as `git status` or a compile.
- **What resets the count?** My suggestion to aj: a source edit since the last run resets it, so repeat runs after a real code change stay allowed. An edit to the check's own script must not reset it, since that is exactly the failure here.
- **How does an agent get past it?** Something like one explicit override for a named flaky failure, recorded in the report. aj decides this.
- **Does a `PreToolUse` hook fire inside a builder subagent, with the session state it needs?** Test this first. If it doesn't, the design changes.
- **What's the switch?** Follow the `HOUSE_RULES_*=off` pattern the other checks use.

## Depends on

Nothing.

## Depended on by

Nothing. It takes in #139, which can close with this.

## Done when

- A builder subagent in a real session is refused its third run of one check with no source edit in between, and the refusal message tells it to stop and report.
- A third run after a real source edit goes through, and an edit to the check's own script doesn't reset the count.
- `scripts/verify.py` passes, the plugin version is bumped, and aj has confirmed it's live in another project.

Part of #406 (Keep work saved and handed off on every reply, so a usage limit never strands it). Design: `docs/plans/2026-11-08-session-handoff-mechanism.html`, step 5.

## What this is

The existing autosave (`event_autosave` in `scripts/house_rules/delegation.py`) saves only subagent branches (`worktree-agent-*`). This step widens it to every branch the main session edits on:

- After a `Write`, `Edit`, `NotebookEdit` or `Bash` call, the hook reads one timestamp file in the `.git` folder. Under 60 seconds since the last save, it only records the file name and stops, with no git process.
- Otherwise it builds a snapshot in a temporary index (a scratch copy of git's staging area): the last commit, changes to tracked files, and new files the agent wrote (the rule from #477, so a stray secrets file is never pushed).
- Each snapshot carries `.house-rules/handoff-facts.md`, written only into the temporary index: branch, last commit, unpushed commits, uncommitted files, design-loop feature and stage, the stage file's issues with labels, and the time.
- The snapshot is a commit no branch points at, stored at `refs/house-rules/autosave/<branch>`, and only that ref is pushed, with a 6-second timeout.
- A detached HEAD is skipped and said once. No `origin`, a push timeout, or any git failure is said in one line. Work-in-progress commits stay on subagent branches only. `HOUSE_RULES_AUTOSAVE=off` still turns it off.

## Depends on

Nothing.

## Depended on by

The turn-end save issue (step 6), step 1 (#407), step 2 (#408, the pickup reads these snapshots), and step 4 (#410).

## Done when

`verify.py` finds a snapshot with the facts file and the edited file after edits on an `AjsAgent/` branch and on `main`, and confirms the branch, the staging area and the folder are unchanged. A second edit within a minute starts no git process. A real edit in a live session puts the ref on GitHub, seen with `git ls-remote`. `verify.py` passes twice with no new failures.

Part of #488 (Handoff overwrite: saves no other folder can erase, pictures that always show, approvals that always register). Design question 1, option A.

## What this is

Today every folder on a branch saves to `refs/house-rules/autosave/<branch>`, so the newest save wins. In the desktop QA, a second clone's save replaced desktop session A's snapshot, and the uncommitted line was no longer on GitHub.

- Each folder gets a random id, written once to `.git/house-rules-folder-id`.
- The save (`event_autosave` and `event_autosave_final` in `scripts/house_rules/delegation.py`) writes and pushes `refs/house-rules/autosave/<branch>/<folder id>` only.
- The pickup (`event_pickup`) lists every other folder's snapshot for the current branch that holds files this folder lacks, newest first, each with its own restore command, `git diff <snap>^ <snap> -- <files> | git apply`. The old single ref is still read, so earlier saves are not stranded.
- The design-loop stage file is never offered for restore (already on the branch, commit d62be1a).
